Heygo · AI Passport · Project summary
Ask the coach during a rest
AI Passport is a small handheld device for skiers. The user sees the data of the last run and hears the AI coach. The user does not take out the phone or remove the gloves. All 18 sprints of the project are complete.

What the team delivered

Increment 1Coach voiceA long press of OK opens the Coach page. The user holds OK and asks a question. The phone does speech-to-text, the AI answer, and text-to-speech. The device plays the answer.
Increment 2Run data and reportLive speed, drop, distance, turns, and time. After each run, a Heygo IQ (0 to 200) and one tip. The device opens the live data page at run start.
Increment 3TurnsThe line of each run, 8 turns on each page. The page shows the speed, angle, and radius of each turn.
Increment 4Phone popupsFall alert, voice notice, issue report, and achievement report. A popup opens at once and counts down 10 s. Any key closes it.


Quick answers



Question
Answer
More




What does the device do?
It controls only the keys, microphone, speaker, and screen. The phone does all analysis and voice work.
Architecture and protocol

7 layers, 3 own tasks, 10 states, and 83 transitions from a flow graph.
Firmware architecture

Scripts make the flow code, fonts, and images. validate.sh builds and checks. You flash the merged image at 0x0.

The app uses 23.4% of the factory partition. Static DRAM is 47.2%. The LVGL pool peak is 76.6%.

Four pages at the same level make a loop. A short press of UP or DOWN changes the page. A long press of OK opens the coach.

25 screens that LVGL renders on the host, and two animations.

One goal in each 4-hour sprint. Evidence shows if the team completed the work. Build, host, and device results are separate.

209 commits on main, from 10-16 18:02 to 10-18 12:05.

A gate runs before each commit. Host tests, screen checks, and the simulator self-test must pass.

English · 简体中文

Firmware

Firmware architecture
The firmware runs on the ESP32-C3. It uses ESP-IDF 5.5.3 and FreeRTOS. The code is in Firmware/. The application is in main/, and the board support is in components/bsp/.

States10
Transitions83
Own tasks3

Sources: Firmware/flows/coach.flow.json (states and transitions), wc -l (lines, BSP included), and Firmware/tests/.
Layers


Figure 9. Firmware layers. The modules with a green frame are plain C. They do not use LVGL or ESP-IDF, and they run in host tests.


The design has two rules:

Keep the logic away from the hardware. The state machine, key mapping, protocol codec, session rules, and ADPCM are plain C. You can test them on a computer.
Compile the canvas into C at build time. The state machine is a graph in coach.flow.json. flowc.py translates it into a C transition table. The device has no graph interpreter, so the runtime cost is zero (tools/flow/flowc.py, file header).

Startup order
Source: main/main.c

01Read the wake causeAfter a key wake, the device ignores keys until the user releases that key (maximum 10 s). Thus, the wake key does not operate the device.
02I2C, screen, and LVGLIf initialization fails, the device logs the SPI pins and stops. The backlight goes to 100%.
03Audio and fuel gaugeES8311 and CW2017. A failure does not stop the startup. The device records the status.
04Start the Coach appMake the queues. Start the voice task, the BLE link, and the coach task.
05Enable the keys lastKey events go into the queue only after the app is ready.


Tasks and queues


Figure 10. Task priorities, stack sizes, and queues. Sources: main/audio/voice.c:20-23, main/link/ble_link.c:27-32, main/coach_app.c:50-52, esp_lvgl_port defaults, and sdkconfig.


The reasons for the priorities:

voice is the highest (7). Audio has one block each 20 ms. A late block causes a gap in the sound (voice.c:23, comment).
ble_tx is next (6). It sends control packets first and audio packets second.
coach is 5. Keys, timers, and link events go into one queue. Thus, the state machine handles one event at a time, without concurrency problems.
LVGL is 4. Drawing can wait for audio and BLE.

Each queue has a fixed size and a fixed overflow rule. A slow link does not make a queue larger (需求文件夹/02-architecture.md, section 5).
State machine
The state machine has 10 states and 83 transitions. flowc.py makes all of them from coach.flow.json into main/generated/coach_flow.c.



Group
States
Description




Pages
LIVE, REPORT, TURNS
Live data, report, and Turns. A short press of UP or DOWN moves in the loop.


Coach
READY, CAPTURE, WAIT_ANSWER, PLAYBACK
Ready, recording, waiting for the answer, and playback.


Popup
POPUP_WAIT, POPUP_PLAY, POPUP_HOLD
Waiting for voice, playing voice, and the 10 s countdown.



Two timers (docs/heygo-changes.md, section 6):

After 20 s in CAPTURE, the timer sends CAPTURE_LIMIT. A recording is 20 s at most.
After 10 s in WAIT_ANSWER, the timer sends AGENT_TIMEOUT.

Only one screen exists at a time. To change the screen, the task loads an empty screen, deletes the old screen, and then builds the new screen. Several screens at the same time do not fit in the LVGL pool.
The page rail is an exception. It is one object on the LVGL top layer that draws the four stops and the thumb. A screen change does not delete it. Thus, the rail uses only one object of the pool on each page (main/ui/page_rail.h, coach_app.c:749).
Audio path

Up · recordingMicrophone to phoneES8311 samples at 16 kHz, 16 bit. The voice task encodes one 164-byte ADPCM block each 20 ms. The block goes to the audio TX queue (8 packets, drop the oldest). ble_tx then sends it as a NimBLE notification.
Down · playbackPhone to speakerNimBLE receives the packet. link_core checks the xid and accepts only the current stream. The block goes to the down queue (8 blocks). play_gate decides when playback starts. The device decodes the block and sends it through I2S and ES8311 to the speaker.


A 20 s question in raw PCM needs 640,000 bytes. The device has no PSRAM. Thus, it sends the recording while it records, and it does not keep the full recording (02-architecture.md, section 5).

简体中文 · English

Firmware

固件架构
固件跑在 ESP32-C3 上，基于 ESP-IDF 5.5.3 和 FreeRTOS。代码在 Firmware/ 下：应用在 main/，板级支持在 components/bsp/。

分层


图 9　固件分层。绿框的模块是纯 C，不依赖 LVGL 和 ESP-IDF，在主机上测试。


设计原则有两条：

逻辑和硬件分开。 状态机、按键映射、协议编解码、会话规则、ADPCM 都写成纯 C，在电脑上就能测。
画布在构建时编译成 C。 状态机画在 coach.flow.json 里，flowc.py 把它翻译成 C 转移表。设备上没有图解释器，运行时开销为零（tools/flow/flowc.py 文件头）。

启动顺序
来源：main/main.c

01查看唤醒原因如果是按键唤醒，先屏蔽按键，等那颗键松手（最多 10 秒），避免唤醒键被当成一次操作。
02I2C、屏幕、LVGL初始化失败时打印 SPI 引脚号后退出。背光开到 100%。
03音频和电量计ES8311 和 CW2017。失败不阻止启动，只记录状态。
04启动 Coach 应用建队列，起 coach、voice、ble_tx 三个任务，开始蓝牙广播。
05最后才打开按键按键事件只在应用就绪后才送进队列。


任务和队列


图 10　任务优先级、栈大小和队列。来源：main/audio/voice.c:20-23、main/link/ble_link.c:27-32、main/coach_app.c:50-52、esp_lvgl_port 默认配置、sdkconfig。


优先级这样排的原因：

voice 最高（7）。 音频每 20 ms 一块，晚了就会断音（voice.c:23 注释）。
ble_tx 其次（6）。 先发控制包，再发音频包。
coach 是 5。 按键、计时器、链路事件都进同一个队列，所以状态机一次只处理一个事件，没有并发问题。
LVGL 是 4。 画屏可以让路给音频和蓝牙。

每个队列大小固定，溢出规则写死。链路慢的时候不扩大队列（需求文件夹/02-architecture.zh_CN.md 第 5 节）。
状态机
10 个状态，83 条转移，全部由 flowc.py 从 coach.flow.json 生成到 main/generated/coach_flow.c。



组
状态
说明




页面
LIVE、REPORT、TURNS
实时数据、报告、弯型。短按 UP/DOWN 循环


教练
READY、CAPTURE、WAIT_ANSWER、PLAYBACK
就绪、录音、等回答、播放


弹窗
POPUP_WAIT、POPUP_PLAY、POPUP_HOLD
等语音、播语音、10 秒倒计时



两个计时器（docs/heygo-changes.zh_CN.md 第 6 节）：

CAPTURE 状态 20 秒后产生 CAPTURE_LIMIT，录音最长 20 秒。
WAIT_ANSWER 状态 10 秒后产生 AGENT_TIMEOUT。

同一时间只存在一个界面。切换时先载入空白界面，删掉旧界面，再建新界面，因为几个界面同时存在会超出 LVGL 内存池。
页面导轨是例外：它是 LVGL 顶层上的一个对象，自己画出四个格子和滑块，换界面时不删除。所以导轨在每个页面上只占内存池里的一个对象（main/ui/page_rail.h、coach_app.c:749）。
音频通路

上行 · 录音麦克风 → 手机ES8311 以 16 kHz、16 bit 采样 → voice 任务每 20 ms 编码成一块 164 字节的 ADPCM → 音频发送队列（8 包，满了丢最旧的）→ ble_tx → NimBLE 通知。
下行 · 播放手机 → 喇叭NimBLE 收包 → link_core 检查 xid，只收当前流 → 下行队列（8 块）→ play_gate 判断何时起播 → 解码 → I2S → ES8311 → 喇叭。


一个 20 秒的问题如果存成裸 PCM，需要 640,000 字节。设备没有 PSRAM，所以录音边录边发，不存整段（02-architecture.zh_CN.md 第 5 节）。

scrum.html.title: Delivery with Scrum
scrum.html.body:
English · 简体中文

Scrum

Delivery with Scrum
This project uses Scrum with a 4-hour sprint. Each sprint has one goal. Evidence, not opinion, shows if the team completed the work.
This chapter describes the Scrum flow as the project used it. Each step gives its source in the repository.

Sprints18
Each sprint4h
User stories25
Requirements25
Decisions34


1. Overview


Figure 13. The Scrum flow. The top row is the delivery path. The bottom row is the change loop. Sources: 需求文件夹/03-scrum-backlog.md and 08-sprint-roadmap.md.


The flow has two paths:

Delivery path. The product goal sets the backlog. Items from the backlog go into sprints. Each sprint delivers one increment and one evidence report.
Change loop. Feedback from the user becomes a decision (D-xx). Then the team changes the requirement documents and orders the backlog again.

2. Product goal and backlog
Product goal

During a run, the skier sees live data on the device. During a rest, the skier asks the AI coach a question by voice and hears the answer. The phone stays in a pocket, and the gloves stay on.

Source: 03-scrum-backlog.md, section 1
Four levels of trace
You can trace each function from the requirement to the sprint. Four documents keep the four kinds of ID:



Level
ID

Example: page rail

TC-24: 40 page changes, the thumb stops in 200 ms each time


Sprint
0 to 17
08-sprint-roadmap and 03
Sprint 16: simulator, firmware, and acceptance



The result: when the team reviews an increment, it can find the related requirement and the test case at once.
Use of story points

Story points compare uncertainty and effort. They are not hours.
The team has no velocity data. Thus, the plan does not assume a velocity.
After the P0 scope became smaller in version 0.4, five P0 stories show "to estimate again".

Source: 03-scrum-backlog.md, sections 2 and 4
3. The 4-hour sprint
Fixed structure

Plan 15Develop 200 minReview 15Retro





Event
Time
Output




Sprint planning
15 min
The team agrees the sprint goal and the tasks. It examines the prerequisites.


Development
200 min
A usable increment that passes the checks of the sprint.


Sprint review
15 min
The team shows the increment and reports the evidence in a fixed format.


Retrospective
10 min
The team records one improvement for the next sprint.



Four rules

If a prerequisite is not met, the sprint does not start. The team does the next sprint that has its prerequisites.
If development takes too long, the team drops tasks at the cut line. Dropped tasks go back to the backlog.
If the team does not reach the sprint goal, the product owner decides the next step. The team does not extend the sprint.
At the end of each sprint, ./tools/validate.sh must exit with code 0.

Source: 08-sprint-roadmap.md, section 1
Example: Sprint 0

Task
Time box
Check




1

60 min
Host tests for block size, round trip, lost blocks, and full-scale input


4
T-4 gate and build

Gate and build pass. The report gives the static RAM.



Cut line: if T-1 and T-2 together take more than 150 minutes, drop T-3. Always do T-4.
Why T-3 can go: protocol document 07 has a raw PCM fallback. Without ADPCM, the team can still test the link.
Result: commit a917aaa delivered all four tasks. The team did not use the cut line. The definition of done closes no story in Sprint 0. Each P0 story still needs a device test and the real phone app.
Source: 06-sprint-0-plan.md, sections 2, 4, and 7
4. Definition of done and evidence
Definition of done
Each increment slice must meet these checks, where they apply:

The user completes the task on a physical AI Passport.
The path uses the real phone app, if the slice needs it.
Host tests, repository checks, and the firmware build all pass.
Device tests pass under recorded conditions.
Chinese text, key actions, mode changes, and cancel behavior pass their tests.
Latency is within the limit of the slice.
The English and Chinese documents describe the same behavior.
The team records each remaining gap.

Important limit: a simulator or a stub cannot replace a device test or a test with the real service.
Source: 03-scrum-backlog.md, section 9
Evidence format
Each sprint review uses this format:
Sprint: N
Sprint Goal: met / not met
Build: PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN
Host tests: PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN
Device tests: PASS / FAIL / PARTIAL / NOT RUN (real phone app or phone_sim)
Unverified: each item that nobody verified

Source: 08-sprint-roadmap.md, section 5
The format keeps "build passed", "host tests passed", and "device tests passed" in three different lines. The Sprint 0 plan names this risk: a person reads a host-only result as a product result, and the status report becomes wrong. The evidence format is the response to that risk (06-sprint-0-plan.md, section 6).
Test conditions



Condition
Content




N1 indoor reference link
One AI Passport, one phone, and the real phone app. The team measures round trip, jitter, and loss. It uses the 95th percentile.


N2 faults
The team tests each fault alone. The faults are a 30 s link break, the app in the background, and a permission failure. Two more are an MTU below 172 and a 5-minute clock offset.


U1 usability
Five adults do one task script with bare hands and with gloves. Nobody helps them during the attempts.



Source: 04-validation-and-decisions.md, section 2
5. Code sprints and acceptance sprints
Each story has two sprints. One sprint makes the code. Another sprint does the acceptance.

Source: 03-scrum-backlog.md, section 4
The reasons for this split:

The board was not available at first. A code sprint needs only the host, so it does not wait for hardware.
An acceptance sprint has its own prerequisites: a board, a phone app that supports protocol 0.2, and five testers. If one is missing, the acceptance sprint does not start.
The team records code and acceptance separately, so the two statuses do not mix. "Code complete" and "acceptance passed" are different statements.

6. How a change enters a sprint
Four-step change flow

Record the feedback and the affected requirements.
The product owner orders the backlog again.
The developers update the estimates.
Record each accepted change in the decision log.

Source: 03-scrum-backlog.md, section 10
All 34 decisions entered the project through this flow. Later, other decisions replaced 6 of them. One decision, D-29 (four pages in a loop), replaced 5. Document 05-decision-amendments gives the reasons.
Example: the order of D-33 and D-34


Figure 14. How a decision becomes firmware. An empty circle is a change after a user review. Source: git log.


Both decisions changed the documents first, then the code, and then the screen images:

Documents first. The team updated documents 01 to 05 in English and Chinese pairs.
Code next. For D-33, the simulator came first (10:47), and the firmware came after the user review (11:49). For D-34, the flow graph, firmware, and simulator came in one set of commits (11:22).
User reviews at any step. D-33 had two review rounds. The first round (11:39) removed the arrows, before the firmware. The second round (12:05) made all stops one color, after the firmware. It changed only page_rail.c (ea4815a).
Screen images last. host_render drew the 25 screens again, so the images in the documents agree with the firmware.

Each duration is the time between the first and the last commit. It is not a measured work time.
7. Engineering methods that support Scrum
Scrum sets the rhythm. These engineering methods make a 4-hour sprint possible:

One sourceOne flow graphcoach.flow.json makes the firmware transition table and the browser simulator. One change updates both.
ReviewOnline simulatorGitHub Pages publishes the simulator. To review an increment, open the page and push the keys. No board is necessary.
DoneAutomatic gatevalidate.sh runs host tests, glyph checks, screen checks, the simulator self-test, and the firmware build. It does the automatic part of the definition of done.
IncrementOne branch for each incrementfeat/report-live-data, feat/turn-view, feat/app-popups, and feat/run-start. Each branch goes into main when its increment is complete.
DocumentsEnglish and Chinese, with asd-ste100D-06 requires a Chinese copy of each English document. ste-lint.py checks the English text. The phone app team reads the same protocol document.
TestsPlain C host testsThe state machine, protocol, and ADPCM are plain C. 33 host tests check the logic without hardware.


The simulator grows with the sprints
Each sprint that changes the screens has a task "update the flow simulator". Thus, the number of self-test checks increases with each increment:
03570105140Sprint 4: 53 checks53Sprint 4Sprint 11: 88 checks88Sprint 11Sprint 13: 104 checks104Sprint 13Sprint 15: 117 checks117Sprint 15Sprint 16 sim: 122 checks122Sprint 16 simSprints 16–17: 128 checks128Sprints 16–17


Sources: sprint results in 08-sprint-roadmap.md, sections 3 and 4. Firmware/docs/heygo-changes.md, sections 12 and 13. Measurements for this book at c865ba8 and 284ab00.
8. Roles



Role
Person in the documents
Actual situation




Product owner
Not assigned
The user made all scope decisions, D-17 included


Scrum Master
Not assigned
—


Developers
Not assigned
One firmware developer. The phone app team works in parallel.



Source: 03-scrum-backlog.md, sections 2 and 3
9. Lessons: what worked and what to improve
What worked

A 4-hour time box with a cut line. If time runs short, the team drops a task. It does not extend the sprint. Sprint 0 and Sprint 2 each had a cut line. Both results say "the team did not use the cut line".
Separate evidence lines. Build, host, device, and unverified items have different lines. Nobody can read a host result as a product result.
A decision log. Each of the 34 decisions has an ID, a status, and a reason. The log also shows which decision replaced which.
Simulator before firmware. The user first reviews the appearance in the browser. The first D-33 change (no arrows) came before the firmware, so the firmware did not need rework for that round.

What to improve



Gap
Evidence
Recommendation




No record of the actual time
The results of Sprints 0, 2, 3, 4, 11, 13, and 15 say that nobody recorded the actual time
Record the start and the end of each sprint. Collect velocity data.


No written retrospective items
The documents contain no retrospective record
Write one improvement after each retrospective. Add it to the next sprint plan.


Roadmap status not current
08-sprint-roadmap still shows "not started" for Sprints 5 to 15
Update the status column after each sprint review.


No assigned roles
Section 3 of 03 shows "not assigned" for all three roles
Name a product owner. Then one person owns the order and the acceptance.


Story points to estimate again
Five P0 stories show "to estimate again"
Estimate them in the next planning event.

简体中文 · English

Scrum

用 Scrum 落地
本项目把 Scrum 压成 4 小时一个 Sprint。每个 Sprint 只有一个目标。完成与否看证据，不看感觉。
本章按项目实际的做法梳理 Scrum 流程，每一步都给出仓库里的出处。

Sprint18
每个 Sprint4小时
用户故事25

1. 全景


图 13　Scrum 流程。上面一行是交付主线，下面一行是变更回路。来源：需求文件夹/03-scrum-backlog.zh_CN.md、08-sprint-roadmap.zh_CN.md。


整个流程有两条线：

交付主线。 产品目标决定待办列表。待办列表的条目排进 Sprint。每个 Sprint 交付一个增量和一份证据。
变更回路。 用户的反馈先写成一条决策（D-xx），再改需求文档，最后重排待办列表。

2. 产品目标和待办列表
产品目标

滑雪者滑行时在设备上看实时数据，休息时用语音向 AI 教练提问并听到回答。手机留在口袋里，手套不用摘。

这样做的作用：评审一个增量时，可以直接查到它对应哪条需求、用哪个用例验收。
故事点的用法

故事点比较不确定性和工作量，不代表小时数。
团队没有速度数据，所以计划不假定速度。
P0 范围在 0.4 版缩小后，5 个 P0 故事标为"待重新估算"。

LVGL 内存池：28 KiB
CONFIG_LV_MEM_SIZE_KILOBYTES=28（sdkconfig.defaults）。扣掉管理开销后可用 25,752 字节。
为什么从 24 KiB 加到 28 KiB。加上页面导轨（D-33）后，24 KiB 的内存池让实时数据页在画速度数字时卡死，当时最大空闲块只有 1,936 字节。内存池改为 28 KiB，多占 4 KiB 系统 RAM（需求文件夹/02-architecture.zh_CN.md:334、05-decision-amendments.zh_CN.md:484）。构建结果对得上：LVGL 的 .bss 从 25,084 字节变成 29,180 字节，正好多 4,096 字节。
